A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PatternLocal research, and their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references despite referring to supplementary material; v3 includes Appendices A–G. Appendix additions therefore establish newly available documentation and evidence, not necessarily newly conducted work.

before.justification: v1 reports original XOR simulations, quantitative XAI-TRIS experiments and qualitative artificial-lesion MRI results in Figures 2, 4 and 5.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports additional EEG evaluations, MRI scores, runtime measurements and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The local surrogate-to-pattern transformation, reconstruction objective in Equation 6, ridge/LASSO options and input representations remain. The Equation 7 correction aligns its first expression with the covariance/variance form already stated in v1. Newly disclosed estimation details, including Appendix B.3's shrinkage discussion, do not establish a revision to the underlying explanation procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds a real EEG left-versus-right fist classification application, extending coverage beyond synthetic images and artificial-lesion MRI. Appendix G.1 also evaluates intermediate mixtures of white and correlated noise, extending the previously reported endpoint noise scenarios.

E2.justification: The named image-benchmark baselines and toy-example comparators remain; Section 4.3's change from eleven to nine methods corrects the count rather than documenting removals. The new EEG evaluation adds raw EEG instances as a physiological reference comparator alongside LIME and PatternLocal (Section 5 and Figure 12).

E3.justification: New protocols include EEG preprocessing, a ShallowFBCSPNet classifier and physiological evaluation using SSD, dipole fits and eLORETA. Appendix G crosses MLP/CNN models with EMD/MSE tuning on 8×8 datasets containing 10,000 samples. Tables 6–7 introduce numerical MRI evaluation using all attributions versus those above 0.9; v1 used that threshold only in displayed overlays.

E4.justification: Where v1 only references supplementary analyses, v3 supplies representation/regularization comparisons, a white-to-correlated-noise sweep and architecture-by-tuning-objective ablations (Figures 8–10 and 13–17). Table 5 adds a matrix-rank diagnosis of high-signal instability, and Tables 6–7 expose sensitivity to attribution thresholding.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly discloses fixed random seeds through pl.seed_everything, while Appendix G.2 specifies that shaded bands represent standard deviations across test images. v1 already displayed standard-deviation bands. Neither version establishes repeated independent runs or an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: v3 supplies extensive numerical results absent from the supplied v1, including MRI tables, runtimes, EEG dipole fits and appendix curves. MRI Table 6 reports EMD 0.166 for PatternLocal versus 0.101 for Integrated Gradients; thresholded Table 7 reports 0.102 versus 0.166. These are newly reported, protocol-dependent rankings, not evidence of a same-setting improvement between versions.

T1.justification: Equation 7 replaces the erroneous feature-second-moment inverse with the surrogate-response second moment. Appendix B.1 derives the ridge solution and states the centering assumption needed for its covariance form. Appendix B.3 adds formal bias, variance, bandwidth and sample-complexity reasoning absent from v1; Appendix B.2 expands the toy derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about mitigating suppressors through local generative explanations remain. v3 adds an abstract claim of physiologically plausible EEG explanations and extends the conclusion's claimed superiority from two image benchmarks to three datasets. This broadens the application claim without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of MRI threshold-dependent rankings, superpixel limitations and high-signal rank deficiency. Appendix F explains why faithfulness metrics can reward suppressor attributions. The EEG discussion acknowledges missing attribution ground truth and interprets physiological plausibility. The original dedicated Limitations paragraph remains substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D supply dataset-generation instructions, network architectures, optimizer and stopping settings, 200-trial tuning budgets, search ranges, software versions, hardware and timing information that v1 relegated to unavailable supplementary material. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the original training settings. The code-access URL is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting references on PredDiff, covariance shrinkage, nonparametric covariance estimation and EEG acquisition, decoding, SSD and source localization. Appendix F extends the positioning against faithfulness-based evaluation. The central relationship to Pattern, PatternNet, PatternAttribution, LIME and SHAP remains.

P1.justification: The main six-section sequence remains. v3 tightens prose, condenses Section 3's explanatory paragraphs, changes latent-variable notation from s to m and replaces vague supplementary references with explicit appendix links. Appendices A–G organize the additional material and provide a notation glossary, while the main narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as an explicit four-step workflow, existing plots are restyled, and MRI panels are updated. v3 adds EEG temporal, spectral and source-localization displays, quantitative MRI and runtime tables, representation comparisons and extensive ablation plots. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves substantial reporting deficiencies in the supplied v1 by making derivations, implementation settings, quantitative MRI results and robustness analyses available, while correcting Equation 7. These additions make the method considerably easier to reproduce and critically assess. The MRI tables reveal weaknesses that temper the retained broad superiority claim, and EEG evidence establishes physiological plausibility rather than attribution correctness. Those limitations remain, but the gains in transparency, technical completeness and assessable evidence are substantial.
